name: CRISPR-SCALE
description: An AUROC reported for a CRISPR guide-efficiency predictor depends on three evaluation choices: how the continuous activity readout is binarised, how much of the library is excluded before scoring, and what the train/test split treats as an independent unit. This work measures how far those choices move the reported figure. One model specification and one out-of-fold prediction vector, assembled from five gene-grouped fold fits, are held fixed while only the evaluation protocol varies. On 18,363 CRISPRi guides the reported AUROC moves from 0.780 at a median split to 0.929 when 90% of the library is excluded, a span of 0.149 [0.137, 0.161], with no change to the model or its predictions. CRISPR-SCALE is the evaluation baseline released with the work: it fixes a splitting scheme, a label definition and an uncertainty procedure as a common reference, so that each choice can be varied against it one at a time.
